explanation shown to learner: Will be + past participle looks forward and focuses on the road.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Will be + 3. forma raugās nākotnē un uzmanību velta ceļam.

task: Use will in the passive: The results ___ on Friday. (announce)
correct answer: will be announced
explanation shown to learner: will be + past participle.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): will be + 3. forma.

task: Change to the passive: They will open the shop at 9.
correct answer: The shop will be opened at 9.
explanation shown to learner: will be + past participle.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): will be + 3. forma.

task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: The prize will be giving to the winner.
wrong options / checks: The meeting will be held in Room 3. | You will be informed by email. | The work will be finished by June.
explanation shown to learner: Use the past participle: The prize will be given to the winner.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Lieto 3. formu: The prize will be given to the winner.

task: You do not want to say who will do the action. Choose the correct option.
correct answer: The files will be checked on Monday.
wrong options / checks: Someone checks the files on Monday. | The files check on Monday. | The files will checking on Monday.
explanation shown to learner: The passive keeps the focus on the files.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Ciešamā kārta saglabā uzmanību uz failiem.

task: Write one sentence about something that will be done in your city or company next year. Use will be + past participle.
correct answer: A new library will be opened in my city next year.
wrong options / checks: must contain: Use *will be* + past participle.
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

task: ___ the new rules be explained to us?
correct answer: Will
wrong options / checks: Do | Are | Have
explanation shown to learner: Passive question: Will + subject + be + past participle.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Jautājums ciešamajā kārtā: Will + teik. priekšmets + be + 3. forma.

task: Which sentence is the passive of 'They will announce the winner tomorrow'?
correct answer: The winner will be announced tomorrow.
wrong options / checks: The winner will announce tomorrow. | The winner is announcing tomorrow. | The winner was announced tomorrow.
explanation shown to learner: will + be + past participle.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): will + be + 3. forma.

task: Use will in the passive: Don't worry. Everything ___ before the guests arrive. (prepare)
correct answer: will be prepared
explanation shown to learner: will be + past participle.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): will be + 3. forma.

task: Change to the passive: We will send the tickets by email.
correct answer: The tickets will be sent by email.
explanation shown to learner: will be + past participle.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): will be + 3. forma.

task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: The class will be cancel.
wrong options / checks: The tickets won't be sold after Friday. | Will the room be cleaned? | You will be told the date soon.
explanation shown to learner: Use the past participle: The class will be cancelled.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Lieto 3. formu: The class will be cancelled.

task: You write an airport announcement. Choose the correct option.
correct answer: Passengers will be informed of any changes.
wrong options / checks: Passengers informing of any changes. | Passengers inform of any changes. | Passengers are informing of any changes.
explanation shown to learner: Announcements often use the passive: will be informed.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Paziņojumos bieži lieto ciešamo kārtu: will be informed.

task: Write two sentences for a notice at work about changes next month. Use will be + past participle.
correct answer: The office will be closed on Monday. All staff will be informed by email.
wrong options / checks: must contain: Use *will be* + past participle. ; Write two sentences.
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

task: Complete the general rule using the zero conditional: If you heat ice, it ___.
correct answer: melts
wrong options / checks: will melt | melting | is melt
explanation shown to learner: Zero conditional: if + present simple, present simple. It describes something that is always true.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Zero conditional: if + Present Simple, Present Simple. Tas apraksta kaut ko, kas ir vienmēr patiess.

task: Match each beginning with the right ending. These are things that are always true.
correct answer: If you heat pure water to its boiling point, = it boils. ; If you don't sleep enough, = you feel tired. ; If the traffic light is red, = cars stop. ; If you mix red and blue paint, = you get purple.
explanation shown to learner: The zero conditional (if + present simple, present simple) is for facts and general rules.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Zero conditional (if + Present Simple, Present Simple) paredzēts faktiem un vispārīgiem noteikumiem.

task: If you ___ the button, the coffee machine ___. (press / start)
correct answer: press / starts
explanation shown to learner: Zero conditional: present simple in both parts.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Zero conditional: abās daļās Present Simple.

task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: If you will heat ice, it melts.
wrong options / checks: If you heat ice, it melts. | If I drink coffee at night, I can't sleep. | If people don't eat, they get hungry.
explanation shown to learner: We do not use will after if. Say: If you heat ice, it melts.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Pēc if nelieto will. Saki: If you heat ice, it melts.

task: A learner wrote: 'If you will mix blue and yellow, you get green.' Choose the correct option.
correct answer: Remove will: 'If you mix blue and yellow, you get green.'
wrong options / checks: Change get to will get: 'If you will mix blue and yellow, you will get green.' | Change mix to mixes. | It is correct. Do not change it.
explanation shown to learner: In the zero conditional both verbs are in the present simple. Will is not used.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Zero conditional abi darbības vārdi ir Present Simple. Will nelieto.

task: Write a sentence about something that always happens in your office or at home. Start with If and use the present simple.
correct answer: If I skip breakfast, I get grumpy by ten.
wrong options / checks: must contain: Start with *If.* ; Do not use *will.* In the zero conditional both parts use the present simple.
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

task: Which word can replace 'if' in a zero conditional? 'If it rains, the street floods.'
correct answer: whenever
wrong options / checks: unless | although | because
explanation shown to learner: In a zero conditional, when or whenever means the same as if: it is always true.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Zero conditional when vai whenever nozīmē to pašu, ko if: tas ir vienmēr patiesi.

task: Which sentence is a zero conditional (always true), not a first conditional (one future situation)?
correct answer: If metal gets hot, it expands.
wrong options / checks: If it gets hot tomorrow, I will go to the beach. | If the shop is closed, we will try the other one. | If I had more time, I would learn Italian.
explanation shown to learner: A zero conditional describes a general truth. The others are about one future situation or an imaginary one.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Zero conditional apraksta vispārēju patiesību. Pārējie teikumi ir par vienu nākotnes situāciju vai iedomātu situāciju.

task: Rewrite with when: If you press this button, the door opens.
correct answer: When you press this button, the door opens.
wrong options / checks: also accepted: The door opens when you press this button.
explanation shown to learner: In a zero conditional, when and whenever can replace if.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Zero conditional if vietā var lietot when un whenever.

task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: If people don't sleep enough, they would be grumpy.
wrong options / checks: If people don't sleep enough, they get grumpy. | Whenever I forget my umbrella, it rains. | If the printer jams, everybody panics.
explanation shown to learner: A general truth uses the present simple in both parts: they get grumpy.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Vispārējai patiesībai abās daļās lieto Present Simple: they get grumpy.

task: Your manager writes a rule: 'If a visitor will arrive, sign them in at reception.' Choose the correct option.
correct answer: If a visitor arrives, sign them in at reception.
wrong options / checks: If a visitor would arrive, sign them in at reception. | If a visitor arrived, sign them in at reception. | If a visitor will arrive, signing them in at reception.
explanation shown to learner: A rule uses if + present simple, then an instruction. We do not use will after if.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Noteikumam lieto if + Present Simple, tad norādījumu. Pēc if nelieto will.

task: Write a rule for a new colleague. Use If + present simple, then an instruction (for example: If the light is red, wait).
correct answer: If the printer jams, ask Marta for help.
wrong options / checks: must contain: Start with *If.* ; Do not use *will* or *would* in a rule like this.
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

task: Choose the correct form: If it ___ tomorrow, we will stay at home.
correct answer: rains
wrong options / checks: will rain | rained | rain
explanation shown to learner: In the if-part we use the present simple, even when we talk about the future.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): If daļā lieto Present Simple, pat runājot par nākotni.

task: What does this sentence mean? 'If you finish the report, I'll buy you a coffee.'
correct answer: It is a promise about a possible future.
wrong options / checks: It is a fact that is always true. | It is about something in the past. | It is about an impossible situation.
explanation shown to learner: The first conditional talks about real, possible future situations. Here it is a promise.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): First conditional runā par reālām, iespējamām nākotnes situācijām. Šeit tas ir solījums.

task: If she ___ late, we ___ without her. (be / start)
correct answer: is / will start
wrong options / checks: also accepted: blank 2: 'll start
explanation shown to learner: First conditional: if + present simple, will + base verb.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): First conditional: if + Present Simple, will + pamatforma.

task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: If I will see him, I will tell him.
wrong options / checks: If you hurry, you'll catch the bus. | She'll be angry if you forget. | If it's sunny, we'll have lunch outside.
explanation shown to learner: No will in the if-part. Say: If I see him, I will tell him.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): If daļā nav will. Saki: If I see him, I will tell him.

task: A friend writes: 'If I will have time, I will call you.' Choose the correct option.
correct answer: If I have time, I'll call you.
wrong options / checks: If I would have time, I will call you. | If I had time, I will call you. | If I will have time, I will call you.
explanation shown to learner: After if we use the present simple: If I have time, I'll call you.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Pēc if lieto Present Simple: If I have time, I'll call you.

task: Write a promise to a colleague. Start with If, use the present simple after if and will in the second part. Put a comma after the if-part.
correct answer: If you cover my shift, I will bring you cake.
wrong options / checks: must contain: Start with *If.* ; Use *will* in the second part. ; Use the present simple after *if* (no *will*), and put a comma after the if-part.
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: if you ask nicely I will help you
wrong options / checks: also accepted: I will help you if you ask nicely
explanation shown to learner: First conditional: if + present simple, will + base verb. The if-part can come first or second.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): First conditional: if + Present Simple, will + pamatforma. If daļa var būt gan pirmā, gan otrā.

task: If you ___ the bus, you ___ be late. (miss / will)
correct answer: miss / will
explanation shown to learner: First conditional: if + present simple, will + base verb.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): First conditional: if + Present Simple, will + pamatforma.

task: Starting now is necessary to finish on time. Complete: We will not finish on time ___ we start now.
correct answer: unless
wrong options / checks: if | when | although
explanation shown to learner: Unless means if ... not: We won't finish unless we start now.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Unless nozīmē if ... not: We won't finish unless we start now.

task: Match each beginning with the most natural ending.
correct answer: If the train is late, = we will take a taxi. ; If you eat that curry, = you will need a glass of milk. ; If you don't back up your files, = you might lose everything. ; Unless it stops raining, = the picnic will be cancelled.
explanation shown to learner: In the first conditional we describe a possible future situation and its likely result.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): First conditional apraksta iespējamu nākotnes situāciju un tās ticamo rezultātu.

task: ___ you finish early, we ___ go for a drink.
correct answer: If / will
wrong options / checks: word bank: If | Until | will | would
explanation shown to learner: First conditional: If + present simple, will + base verb.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): First conditional: If + Present Simple, will + pamatforma.

task: I'll call you as soon as I ___ at the station. (arrive)
correct answer: arrive
explanation shown to learner: After as soon as, when and before we use the present simple for the future.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Pēc as soon as, when un before nākotnei lieto Present Simple.

task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: I'll text you when I will get home.
wrong options / checks: I'll text you as soon as I get home. | If you don't hurry, you'll miss it. | We won't go unless the weather improves.
explanation shown to learner: After when, as soon as, if and unless we use the present simple for the future: when I get home.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Pēc when, as soon as, if un unless nākotnei lieto Present Simple: when I get home.

task: You want to warn a friend who keeps forgetting his password. Choose the correct option.
correct answer: If you forget it again, you'll be locked out.
wrong options / checks: If you will forget it again, you'll be locked out. | If you forgot it again, you'll be locked out. | If you forget it again, you locked out.
explanation shown to learner: A warning uses if + present simple, then will + base verb.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Brīdinājumam lieto if + Present Simple, tad will + pamatforma.

task: Write a sentence with unless about something you must do to avoid a problem.
correct answer: Unless I leave now, I will miss my train.
wrong options / checks: must contain: Use *unless.*
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

task: Which sentence is a correct first conditional?
correct answer: If it snows tonight, the office will close.
wrong options / checks: If it will snow tonight, the office closes. | If it snowed tonight, the office will close. | If it snows tonight, the office would close.
explanation shown to learner: First conditional: if + present simple, will + base verb.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): First conditional: if + Present Simple, will + pamatforma.

task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: unless you hurry you will miss the train
wrong options / checks: also accepted: you will miss the train unless you hurry
explanation shown to learner: Unless means if ... not. After unless we use the present simple.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Unless nozīmē if ... not. Pēc unless lieto Present Simple.

task: Choose the correct form: I'll call you as soon as I ___.
correct answer: arrive
wrong options / checks: will arrive | would arrive | arrived
explanation shown to learner: After as soon as we use the present simple for the future.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Pēc as soon as nākotnei lieto Present Simple.

task: What is the difference? A: 'If you're late, I'll be angry.' B: 'If you're late, I might be angry.'
correct answer: A is more certain than B.
wrong options / checks: B is more certain than A. | A is about the past and B is about the future. | There is no difference.
explanation shown to learner: Will is certain. Might, may and could show that the result is possible but not sure.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Will ir drošs. Might, may un could rāda, ka rezultāts ir iespējams, bet nav drošs.

task: Rewrite with unless: If you don't practise, you won't improve.
correct answer: Unless you practise, you won't improve.
wrong options / checks: also accepted: Unless you practice, you won't improve. | You won't improve unless you practise. | You won't improve unless you practice.
explanation shown to learner: Unless means if ... not, so the clause after it is usually positive: Unless you practise, you won't improve.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Unless nozīmē if ... not, tāpēc teikums aiz tā parasti ir apgalvojošs: Unless you practise, you won't improve.

task: Which sentence means the same as: 'If you don't hurry, you will be late.'?
correct answer: Unless you hurry, you will be late.
wrong options / checks: If you hurry, you will be late. | Unless you hurry, you will be on time. | You will be on time unless you hurry.
explanation shown to learner: Unless you hurry means if you do not hurry, so the warning stays the same: you will be late. The other sentences change who must hurry or what happens.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Unless you hurry nozīmē if you do not hurry. Papildu noliegums maina nosacījumu un vairs neizsaka doto brīdinājumu. Noliegums pēc unless var būt pareizs, ja ir domāta cita nozīme.

task: In an email to a client you want to sound confident but polite. Choose the correct option.
correct answer: If you send us the documents today, we will process your request by Friday.
wrong options / checks: If you will send us the documents today, we will process your request by Friday. | If you sent us the documents today, we will process your request by Friday. | If you send us the documents today, we would process your request by Friday.
explanation shown to learner: Real future condition: if + present simple, will + base verb.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Reāls nākotnes nosacījums: if + Present Simple, will + pamatforma.

task: Write a sentence with in case (for example: I'll take an umbrella in case it rains). Use the present simple after in case.
correct answer: I'll take a charger in case my phone dies.
wrong options / checks: must contain: Use *in case.* ; After *in case* we use the present simple: *in case it rains.*
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

task: Choose the correct form: If I ___ a million euros, I would buy a boat.
correct answer: had
wrong options / checks: have | will have | would have
explanation shown to learner: Second conditional: if + past simple, would + base verb.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Second conditional: if + Past Simple, would + pamatforma.

task: What does this sentence mean? 'If I were taller, I would play basketball.'
correct answer: I am not tall, so I don't play basketball.
wrong options / checks: I am tall and I play basketball. | I will be taller soon. | I played basketball when I was young.
explanation shown to learner: The second conditional talks about unreal or unlikely situations. The verb is past, but the meaning is now.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Second conditional runā par nereālām vai maz ticamām situācijām. Darbības vārds ir pagātnē, bet nozīme ir par tagadni.

task: If I ___ the boss, I ___ cancel all Monday meetings. (be)
correct answer: were / would
wrong options / checks: also accepted: blank 1: was; blank 2: 'd
explanation shown to learner: Second conditional: if + past simple (were), would + base verb.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Second conditional: if + Past Simple (were), would + pamatforma.

task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: If I will win the lottery, I would buy an island.
wrong options / checks: If I won the lottery, I would buy an island. | If I were you, I wouldn't do that. | What would you do if you saw a ghost?
explanation shown to learner: The if-part uses the past simple, not will: If I won the lottery, ...
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): If daļā lieto Past Simple, nevis will: If I won the lottery, ...

task: Your friend can't decide whether to quit and become a baker. You give advice. Choose the correct option.
correct answer: If I were you, I would talk to a few bakers first.
wrong options / checks: If I am you, I will talk to a few bakers first. | If I would be you, I talk to a few bakers first. | If I was you, I will talk to a few bakers first.
explanation shown to learner: For advice we say: If I were you, I would + base verb.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Padomam saka: If I were you, I would + pamatforma.

task: Write a sentence about what you would do if you won a free holiday. Start with If, use the past simple after if and would in the second part.
correct answer: If I won a free holiday, I would go to Iceland.
wrong options / checks: must contain: Start with *If.* ; Use *would* in the second part. ; Use the past simple after *if* (not *would*): *If I won a holiday, I would go to Iceland.*
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

task: If I ___ a cat, I ___ sleep all day.
correct answer: were / would
wrong options / checks: word bank: were | would | will | being
explanation shown to learner: Second conditional: if + were / past simple, would + base verb.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Second conditional: if + were / Past Simple, would + pamatforma.

task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: if I had more time I would learn the piano
wrong options / checks: also accepted: I would learn the piano if I had more time
explanation shown to learner: Second conditional: if + past simple, would + base verb. The if-part can come first or second.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Second conditional: if + Past Simple, would + pamatforma. If daļa var būt gan pirmā, gan otrā.

task: Which question is correct? '___ you do if you lost your passport abroad?'
correct answer: What would
wrong options / checks: What will | What did | What are
explanation shown to learner: Second conditional question: What would you do if you + past simple?
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Second conditional jautājums: What would you do if you + Past Simple?

task: Match each sentence with its meaning.
correct answer: If I had a car, I would drive to work. = I don't have a car. ; If I have a car next year, I will drive to work. = Maybe I'll buy one. ; If I had had a car, I would have driven to work. = I didn't have a car then. ; If you heat ice, it melts. = This is always true.
explanation shown to learner: Zero: always true. First: real future. Second: unreal now. Third: unreal past.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Zero: vienmēr patiess. First: reāla nākotne. Second: nereāls tagad. Third: nereāls pagātnē.

task: Rewrite as a second conditional: I don't have enough money, so I can't buy a new laptop.
correct answer: If I had enough money, I could buy a new laptop.
wrong options / checks: also accepted: If I had enough money, I would buy a new laptop. | If I had enough money, I'd buy a new laptop. | I could buy a new laptop if I had enough money. | I would buy a new laptop if I had enough money. | I'd buy a new laptop if I had enough money.
explanation shown to learner: Second conditional: if + past simple, would / could + base verb.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Second conditional: if + Past Simple, would / could + pamatforma.

task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: If I would have more free time, I would join a choir.
wrong options / checks: If I had more free time, I would join a choir. | I would join a choir if I had more free time. | If I had more free time, I might join a choir.
explanation shown to learner: Do not use would in the if-part. Say: If I had more free time, ...
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): If daļā nelieto would. Saki: If I had more free time, ...

task: You advise a manager politely. Choose the correct option.
correct answer: If I were you, I would speak to the team before the meeting.
wrong options / checks: If I were you, I will speak to the team before the meeting. | If I am you, I would speak to the team before the meeting. | If you were me, I would speak to the team before the meeting.
explanation shown to learner: Advice: If I were you, I would + base verb.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Padoms: If I were you, I would + pamatforma.

task: Write a sentence about an unlikely job you would like. Use if + past simple and would.
correct answer: If I were a pilot, I would fly to Iceland every weekend.
wrong options / checks: must contain: Start with *If.* ; Use *would* in the second part. ; Use the past simple after *if* (not *would*): *If I were a pilot, I would fly.*
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

task: Which is correct? 'If I ___ you, I'd think twice about that offer.'
correct answer: were
wrong options / checks: am | would be | had been
explanation shown to learner: In careful English we use were for all persons after if in the second conditional.

task: What is the difference? A: 'If I had time, I would help.' B: 'If I had time, I might help.'
correct answer: B is less certain than A.
wrong options / checks: A is less certain than B. | A is about the past and B about the future. | There is no difference in meaning.
explanation shown to learner: Would shows the result is certain in that imaginary situation. Might shows it is only possible.

task: If the company ___ more flexible hours, people ___ happier. (offer / be)
correct answer: offered / would be
wrong options / checks: also accepted: blank 1: were to offer; blank 2: 'd be
explanation shown to learner: Second conditional: if + past simple (or were to + base verb), would + base verb.

task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: If I would know the answer, I would tell you.
wrong options / checks: If I knew the answer, I would tell you. | If I knew the answer, I'd tell you. | I would tell you if I knew the answer.
explanation shown to learner: Would does not go in the if-part. Say: If I knew the answer, I would tell you.

task: You write a polite request in a formal email. Choose the correct option.
correct answer: I would be grateful if you could send me the report by Friday.
wrong options / checks: I would be grateful if you will send me the report by Friday. | I would grateful if you could send me the report by Friday. | I would be grateful if you could to send me the report by Friday.
explanation shown to learner: A polite request: I would be grateful if you could + base verb.

task: Write advice for a colleague who works too much. Start with If I were you and use would.
correct answer: If I were you, I would switch off my phone after seven.
wrong options / checks: must contain: Start with *If I were you.* ; Use *would* in the second part.
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.

topic: Third conditional (if + had done, would have done)
task: Choose the correct form: If I ___ earlier, I wouldn't have missed the train.
correct answer: had left
wrong options / checks: left | would have left | have left
explanation shown to learner: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Third conditional: if + Past Perfect, would have + 3. forma.

topic: Third conditional (if + had done, would have done)
task: 'If we had booked earlier, we would have got a cheaper flight.' What really happened?
correct answer: We did not book earlier.
wrong options / checks: We booked early and got a cheap flight. | We will book early next time. | We never fly.
explanation shown to learner: The third conditional imagines a different past. We did not book earlier, and the imagined earlier booking would have been cheaper.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Third conditional izsaka iedomātu pagātnes situāciju. Mēs nerezervējām agrāk; ja būtu rezervējuši agrāk, cena būtu bijusi zemāka.

topic: Third conditional (if + had done, would have done)
task: If you ___ me about the meeting, I ___ there. (tell / be)
correct answer: had told / would have been
wrong options / checks: also accepted: blank 2: 'd have been
explanation shown to learner: Third conditional: if + had + past participle, would have + past participle.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Third conditional: if + had + 3. forma, would have + 3. forma.

topic: Third conditional (if + had done, would have done)
task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: If I would have known, I would have called you.
wrong options / checks: If I had known, I would have called you. | I would have called you if I had known. | If I hadn't known, I wouldn't have called you.
explanation shown to learner: Do not use would in the if-part. Say: If I had known, ...
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): If daļā nelieto would. Saki: If I had known, ...

topic: Third conditional (if + had done, would have done)
task: A colleague forgot to save a file and lost two hours of work. Choose the correct third conditional comment.
correct answer: If you had saved it every ten minutes, you wouldn't have lost so much work.
wrong options / checks: If you saved it every ten minutes, you wouldn't have lost so much work. | If you had saved it every ten minutes, you won't lose so much work. | If you would have saved it every ten minutes, you wouldn't have lost so much work.
explanation shown to learner: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Third conditional: if + Past Perfect, would have + 3. forma.

topic: Third conditional (if + had done, would have done)
task: Write a sentence about a mistake you made once (for example, a missed bus). Start with If I had and use would have or would not have (wouldn't have).
correct answer: If I had checked the time, I wouldn't have missed the bus.
wrong options / checks: must contain: Start with *If I had.* ; Use *would have* + past participle in the second part.
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

topic: Third conditional (if + had done, would have done)
task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: if I had known about the party I would have bought a gift
wrong options / checks: also accepted: I would have bought a gift if I had known about the party
explanation shown to learner: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Third conditional: if + Past Perfect, would have + 3. forma.

topic: Third conditional (if + had done, would have done)
task: Choose the correct form: She would have passed the exam if she ___ harder.
correct answer: had studied
wrong options / checks: studied | would study | has studied
explanation shown to learner: Third conditional: would have + past participle, if + past perfect.

topic: Third conditional (if + had done, would have done)
task: 'If he hadn't been so rude, we might have signed the deal.' What does 'might have' show?
correct answer: The result was possible but not certain.
wrong options / checks: The result was certain. | The result was impossible. | The deal was signed.
explanation shown to learner: Might have and could have show a possible result of the imagined past. Would have shows a certain one.

topic: Third conditional (if + had done, would have done)
task: Rewrite as a third conditional: I didn't see the sign, so I parked there and got a fine.
correct answer: If I had seen the sign, I wouldn't have parked there.
wrong options / checks: also accepted: If I had seen the sign, I wouldn't have got a fine. | If I had seen the sign, I would not have got a fine. | If I had seen the sign, I wouldn't have gotten a fine. | If I had seen the sign, I wouldn't have been fined. | If I had seen the sign, I would not have parked there. | I wouldn't have parked there if I had seen the sign. | I wouldn't have got a fine if I had seen the sign. | I would not have got a fine if I had seen the sign. | I wouldn't have gotten a fine if I had seen the sign. | I wouldn't have been fined if I had seen the sign. | I would not have parked there if I had seen the sign.
explanation shown to learner: Third conditional: if + had seen, would not have + past participle.

topic: Third conditional (if + had done, would have done)
task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: If the team has been better prepared, we would have won.
wrong options / checks: If the team had been better prepared, we would have won. | We would have won if the team had been better prepared. | If the team hadn't been so tired, we might have won.
explanation shown to learner: The if-part needs the past perfect: had been, not has been.

topic: Third conditional (if + had done, would have done)
task: You write a polite criticism in a work review. Choose the correct option.
correct answer: If you had told us earlier, we could have adjusted the schedule.
wrong options / checks: If you told us earlier, we could have adjusted the schedule. | If you had told us earlier, we could adjust have the schedule. | If you would tell us earlier, we could have adjusted the schedule.
explanation shown to learner: Third conditional with could have: if + past perfect, could have + past participle.

topic: Third conditional (if + had done, would have done)
task: Write a sentence about a decision that changed your life. Start with If I hadn't and use would have or would not have (wouldn't have).
correct answer: If I hadn't joined that course, I wouldn't have met my best friend.
wrong options / checks: must contain: Start with *If I hadn't.* ; Use *would have* + past participle in the second part.
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.

topic: Third conditional (if + had done, would have done)
task: Imagine a different past using the third conditional: 'If she ___ the warning, she ___ the accident.'
correct answer: had heard / would have avoided
wrong options / checks: heard / would avoid | had heard / would avoid | would have heard / had avoided
explanation shown to learner: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.

topic: Third conditional (if + had done, would have done)
task: What is the difference? A: 'If you had asked, I would have helped.' B: 'If you asked, I would help.'
correct answer: A is about the past (you did not ask). B is about now or the future.
wrong options / checks: A is about now. B is about the past. | A is about the future. B is about the past. | There is no difference.
explanation shown to learner: Third conditional = past, unreal. Second conditional = present or future, unreal.

topic: Third conditional (if + had done, would have done)
task: If he ___ (not / drive) so fast, he ___ (not / lose) his licence.
correct answer: hadn't been driving / wouldn't have lost
wrong options / checks: also accepted: blank 1: had not been driving | hadn't driven | had not driven; blank 2: would not have lost | 'd not have lost
explanation shown to learner: Negative third conditional: hadn't been driving (or hadn't driven), then wouldn't have lost.

topic: Third conditional (if + had done, would have done)
task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: If I'd have known about the traffic, I would've left earlier.
wrong options / checks: If I'd known about the traffic, I would've left earlier. | If I had known about the traffic, I would have left earlier. | Had I known about the traffic, I would have left earlier.
explanation shown to learner: In standard written English use had + past participle in this if-clause: If I had known. Had I known is a correct inverted alternative. If I'd have known occurs informally but is not the standard form.

topic: Third conditional (if + had done, would have done)
task: You express regret in a formal apology. Choose the correct option.
correct answer: If I had realised the impact of my decision, I would have acted differently.
wrong options / checks: If I realised the impact of my decision, I would have acted differently. | If I would have realised the impact of my decision, I acted differently. | If I had realise the impact of my decision, I would have acted differently.
explanation shown to learner: Formal regret about the past: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.

topic: Third conditional (if + had done, would have done)
task: Write a sentence about what would have happened in history if one thing had been different (for example a famous discovery).
correct answer: If Alexander Fleming hadn't left his dish uncovered, penicillin might not have been discovered.
wrong options / checks: must contain: Use *if.* ; Use the past perfect (*had / hadn't*) in the if-part. ; Use *would / might / could have* + past participle in the result.
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.

task: Which sentence is a mixed conditional (past condition, present result)?
correct answer: If I had taken that job, I would be rich now.
wrong options / checks: If I took that job, I would be rich. | If I had taken that job, I would have been rich. | If I take that job, I will be rich.
explanation shown to learner: Mixed conditional: if + past perfect (past), would + base verb (now).

task: 'If I hadn't moved to Riga, I wouldn't have this job now.' What does it mean?
correct answer: I moved to Riga, so I have this job today.
wrong options / checks: I didn't move to Riga, so I have no job. | I will move to Riga. | I have this job, but I never lived in Riga.
explanation shown to learner: A past action (moved) has a result in the present (have this job).

task: If I ___ English at school, I ___ fluent now. (learn / be)
correct answer: had learned / would be
wrong options / checks: also accepted: blank 1: had learnt; blank 2: 'd be
explanation shown to learner: Mixed conditional: if + had + past participle, would + base verb.

task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: If I would have studied medicine, I would be a doctor now.
wrong options / checks: If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now. | If I'd studied medicine, I'd be a doctor now. | I would be a doctor now if I had studied medicine.
explanation shown to learner: Do not use would in the if-part: If I had studied medicine, ...

task: You explain why someone is tired today because of last night. Choose the correct option.
correct answer: If I hadn't stayed up so late, I wouldn't be so tired now.
wrong options / checks: If I didn't stay up so late, I wouldn't have been so tired now. | If I hadn't stayed up so late, I wouldn't have been so tired now. | If I wouldn't have stayed up so late, I wasn't so tired now.
explanation shown to learner: Past cause, present result: if + past perfect, would + base verb.

task: Write a sentence about how a past decision affects you now. Start with If I had and use would + base verb (not would have).
correct answer: If I had gone to bed earlier, I would feel better now.
wrong options / checks: must contain: Start with *If I had.* ; Use *would* + base verb for the present result.
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.

task: Complete: 'If I weren't so shy, I ___ asked her out last year.'
correct answer: would have
wrong options / checks: would | will have | had
explanation shown to learner: Present quality (weren't), past result (would have asked): if + past simple, would have + past participle.

task: 'If she were more organised, she wouldn't have missed the deadline.' What does it say?
correct answer: She is not organised in general, and that caused the missed deadline.
wrong options / checks: She is organised, but she missed the deadline. | She will be organised next week. | She did not miss the deadline.
explanation shown to learner: A present, permanent quality caused a past result.

task: Rewrite as a mixed conditional: He didn't take the job, so he isn't living in Paris now.
correct answer: If he had taken the job, he would be living in Paris now.
wrong options / checks: also accepted: If he'd taken the job, he'd be living in Paris now. | He would be living in Paris now if he had taken the job. | He'd be living in Paris now if he'd taken the job.
explanation shown to learner: Mixed conditional: if + had + past participle, would + base verb.

task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: If I am more careful, I wouldn't have lost my keys.
wrong options / checks: If I were more careful, I wouldn't have lost my keys. | If I had been more careful, I wouldn't have lost my keys. | If I hadn't been so careless, I wouldn't be searching now.
explanation shown to learner: Do not use am in an unreal condition. Say: If I were more careful, ...

task: A colleague says: 'If I had a better memory, I would have remembered your birthday.' Choose the correct comment about the grammar.
correct answer: It is a mixed conditional: a present quality (memory) with a past result.
wrong options / checks: It is a first conditional about the future. | It is a zero conditional about a fact. | It is a third conditional because of would have.
explanation shown to learner: The if-part is past simple (present quality). The result is would have + past participle (past).

task: Write a mixed conditional sentence: a present quality + a past result (for example: If I were braver, I would have ...).
correct answer: If I were more patient, I wouldn't have shouted at the printer yesterday.
wrong options / checks: must contain: Use *if.* ; Use *would have* + past participle for the past result.
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.

task: Which sentence uses inversion in a mixed conditional?
correct answer: Had I taken that job, I would be rich now.
wrong options / checks: Had I take that job, I would be rich now. | If had I taken that job, I would be rich now. | Did I take that job, I would be rich now.
explanation shown to learner: Inversion replaces if with Had + subject + past participle.

task: 'Were I more experienced, I would have applied for the director role last year.' What does 'Were I' replace?
correct answer: If I were
wrong options / checks: If I had been | If I will be | Unless I was
explanation shown to learner: Were I = If I were. It is formal.

task: Rewrite with inversion: If I had listened to my accountant, I wouldn't be in this mess now.
correct answer: Had I listened to my accountant, I wouldn't be in this mess now.
wrong options / checks: also accepted: Had I listened to my accountant, I'd not be in this mess now. | I wouldn't be in this mess now had I listened to my accountant. | I'd not be in this mess now had I listened to my accountant.
explanation shown to learner: Inversion: Had + subject + past participle replaces if I had + past participle.

task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: Hadn't I taken that job, I wouldn't be living here now.
wrong options / checks: Had I not taken that job, I wouldn't be living here now. | Had I taken that job, I would be rich now. | Were I braver, I would have said no.
explanation shown to learner: Negative inversion is Had I not ..., not Hadn't I ...

task: You write a formal report about a past failure with a present effect. Choose the correct option.
correct answer: Had the contract been checked properly, we would not be facing these penalties now.
wrong options / checks: If the contract had checked properly, we would not be facing these penalties now. | Had the contract been checked properly, we wouldn't facing these penalties now. | Had checked the contract properly, we would not be facing these penalties now.
explanation shown to learner: Passive inversion: Had + object + been + past participle.

task: Write a mixed conditional with inversion about a past decision and its effect today. Start with Had I.
correct answer: Had I saved more when I was young, I would be more relaxed about money today.
wrong options / checks: must contain: Start with *Had I.* ; Use *would* in the second part.
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.

task: Which sentence means the same as 'If you should need any help, call me'?
correct answer: Should you need any help, call me.
wrong options / checks: Did you need any help, call me. | Would you need any help, call me. | Need you any help, call me.
explanation shown to learner: Should + subject + base verb is a formal way to say if you should ...

task: What does 'unless' mean in 'We'll start unless it rains'?
correct answer: if it does not rain
wrong options / checks: if it rains | because it rains | although it rains
explanation shown to learner: Unless = if ... not.

task: Rewrite with unless: You will not get a refund if you don't have a receipt.
correct answer: You will not get a refund unless you have a receipt.
wrong options / checks: also accepted: Unless you have a receipt, you will not get a refund.
explanation shown to learner: Unless replaces if ... not, so the verb after unless is positive.

task: Which sentence means the same as: 'If you don't hurry, we will miss the flight.'?
correct answer: Unless you hurry, we will miss the flight.
wrong options / checks: If you hurry, we will miss the flight. | Unless you hurry, we will catch the flight. | We will catch the flight unless you hurry.
explanation shown to learner: Unless you hurry means if you do not hurry, so the warning stays the same: we will miss the flight. The other sentences change who must hurry or what happens.

task: Choose the most formal option.
correct answer: Should you require further information, please contact our office.
wrong options / checks: If you want more info, ring us. | If you need more information, just call us. | Call us if you need more info.
explanation shown to learner: Should + subject + verb is formal and common in business letters.

task: Write a sentence with 'provided that' or 'as long as' to give a condition for a favour.
correct answer: You can borrow my laptop as long as you bring it back by Friday.
wrong options / checks: must contain: Use *provided that* or *as long as.*
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.

task: Which sentence expresses regret about the present?
correct answer: I wish I lived closer to the sea.
wrong options / checks: I wish I had lived closer to the sea. | I wish I will live closer to the sea. | I wish I would live closer to the sea.
explanation shown to learner: wish + past simple = regret about a present situation.

task: 'I wish you would stop clicking your pen.' What does 'wish + would' show?
correct answer: annoyance about someone's repeated behaviour
wrong options / checks: regret about the past | a plan for the future | a polite offer
explanation shown to learner: wish + would is for things that annoy us and that we want to change.

task: I wish I ___ that email yesterday. Now everyone knows.
correct answer: hadn't sent
wrong options / checks: word bank: hadn't sent | didn't send | wouldn't send | haven't sent
explanation shown to learner: wish + past perfect = regret about the past.

task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: If only I would have saved more money when I was young.
wrong options / checks: If only I had saved more money when I was young. | I wish I had saved more money when I was young. | If only I saved more money now.
explanation shown to learner: If only + past perfect is used for regret about the past. Not would have.

task: You give a speech about a past failure. Choose the correct option.
correct answer: If only we had listened to the warning signs, we would not be in this position.
wrong options / checks: If only we would have listened to the warning signs, we would not be in this position. | If only we listened to the warning signs, we would not be in this position. | If only we had listen to the warning signs, we would not be in this position.
explanation shown to learner: If only + had + past participle, then would + base verb for the present result.

task: Write a sentence with 'I wish' or 'If only' about something you regret from last year.
correct answer: I wish I had started learning Spanish last year.
wrong options / checks: must contain: Use *I wish* or *If only.* ; For a regret about the past use the past perfect (*had / hadn't*).
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.

task: Report it. Move the verb one step back: 'I am tired,' she said. → She said she ___ tired.
correct answer: was
wrong options / checks: is | am | will be
explanation shown to learner: In reported speech the verb usually goes one step back in time: am / is → was.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Netiešajā runā darbības vārds parasti iet vienu soli atpakaļ laikā: am / is → was.

task: Match each sentence with its report.
correct answer: 'I work in a bank,' she said. = She said she worked in a bank. ; 'I'm working late,' she said. = She said she was working late. ; 'I finished the report,' she said. = She said she had finished the report. ; 'I can come,' she said. = She said she could come.
explanation shown to learner: With a past reporting verb the tense often goes one step back: work → worked, am working → was working, finished → had finished, can → could. It is not always needed, for example when the fact is still true.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Pēc darbības vārda pagātnē laiks bieži iet vienu soli atpakaļ: work → worked, am working → was working, finished → had finished, can → could. Tas nav vienmēr vajadzīgs, piemēram, ja fakts joprojām ir patiess.

task: 'I don't like coffee,' Mark said. → Mark said he ___ coffee. (not / like)
correct answer: didn't like
wrong options / checks: also accepted: did not like
explanation shown to learner: The present simple moves back to the past simple: don't like → didn't like.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Present Simple pāriet uz Past Simple: don't like → didn't like.

task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: He said me he was tired.
wrong options / checks: He told me he was tired. | He said he was tired. | He said to me that he was tired.
explanation shown to learner: After said we do not use a person directly. Use told me, or said to me.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Pēc said personu tieši nelieto. Lieto told me vai said to me.

task: Report this: 'I can't come to the meeting,' Jon said. Choose the correct option.
correct answer: Jon said he couldn't come to the meeting.
wrong options / checks: Jon said I couldn't come to the meeting. | Jon said he can't came to the meeting. | Jon said he couldn't to come to the meeting.
explanation shown to learner: can't → couldn't, and I → he (Jon is talking about himself).
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): can't → couldn't, un I → he (Jons runā par sevi).

task: Report this sentence. 'I'm learning Spanish,' Elena said. Start with Elena said.
correct answer: Elena said she was learning Spanish.
wrong options / checks: must contain: Start with *Elena said.* ; Change *I* to *she.* ; *am learning* becomes *was learning.*
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

task: Use backshift. Direct: 'I have finished.' Reported: He said he ___ finished.
correct answer: had
wrong options / checks: has | have | was
explanation shown to learner: The present perfect (have finished) goes back to the past perfect (had finished).
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Present Perfect (have finished) pāriet uz Past Perfect (had finished).

task: What usually happens to 'tomorrow' and 'now' in reported speech?
correct answer: They change to 'the next day' and 'then'.
wrong options / checks: They stay the same. | They change to 'yesterday' and 'always'. | They disappear.
explanation shown to learner: Time words move too: now → then, today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, yesterday → the day before.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Mainās arī laika vārdi: now → then, today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, yesterday → the day before.

task: Report this: 'I'm leaving now,' Kate said.
correct answer: Kate said she was leaving then.
wrong options / checks: also accepted: Kate said that she was leaving then. | Kate said she was leaving at that moment. | Kate said that she was leaving at that moment. | Kate said she was leaving at that time. | Kate said that she was leaving at that time. | Kate said she was leaving right then. | Kate said she was leaving now. | Kate said that she was leaving now. | Kate said she was leaving. | Kate said that she was leaving.
explanation shown to learner: I → she, am leaving → was leaving, now → then.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): I → she, am leaving → was leaving, now → then.

task: You are reporting past statements using backshift. Which sentence has NOT backshifted its future verb?
correct answer: She said she will call me the next day.
wrong options / checks: She said she would call me the next day. | She told me she had finished the report. | He said he was working at home that day.
explanation shown to learner: In this exercise, will backshifts to would. Without that instruction, keeping will can be possible if the promise is still relevant to the future.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Šajā uzdevumā will jāmaina uz would. Citā kontekstā will var saglabāt, ja solījums joprojām attiecas uz nākotni.

task: You report a message to your manager: 'We are almost ready,' the team said. Choose the correct option.
correct answer: The team told me they were almost ready.
wrong options / checks: The team told me we were almost ready. | The team said me they were almost ready. | The team told they were almost ready.
explanation shown to learner: told needs a person (told me). We becomes they, and are goes back to were.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): told vajag personu (told me). We kļūst par they, un are pāriet uz were.

task: Report what a colleague said yesterday: 'I'll send the file tomorrow.' Start with He said.
correct answer: He said he would send the file the next day.
wrong options / checks: must contain: Start with *He said.* ; *will* becomes *would.* ; *tomorrow* changes: *the next day* (or *today*).
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: she said she was leaving at six that day
wrong options / checks: also accepted: she said she was leaving that day at six
explanation shown to learner: Reported speech: said + subject + backshifted verb. Today becomes that day.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Netiešā runa: said + teik. priekšmets + darbības vārds, kas iet soli atpakaļ. Today kļūst par that day.

task: Which modal normally stays in the same form when we backshift a report?
correct answer: might
wrong options / checks: can | will | may
explanation shown to learner: can → could, will → would, must → had to. Might, would, could, should and ought to stay the same.

task: 'The Earth goes round the Sun,' the teacher said. Which version is also correct?
correct answer: Report: The teacher said the Earth goes round the Sun. Reason: it is always true, so the tense can stay.
wrong options / checks: Report: The teacher said the Earth went round the Sun. Reason: it must go back, because said is in the past. | Report: The teacher said the Earth had gone round the Sun. Reason: it must go back two steps. | Report: The teacher said the Earth goes round the Sun. Reason: this is wrong, because reported speech always changes the tense.
explanation shown to learner: When the fact is still true, the tense does not have to go back.

task: Report this: 'You must finish by Friday,' my boss said.
correct answer: My boss said I had to finish by Friday.
wrong options / checks: also accepted: My boss said that I had to finish by Friday. | My boss told me I had to finish by Friday. | My boss told me that I had to finish by Friday. | My boss said I must finish by Friday. | My boss told me I must finish by Friday. | My boss said that I must finish by Friday. | My boss told me that I must finish by Friday.
explanation shown to learner: must can become had to. It can also stay must when the duty is still there.

task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: She told that she would be late.
wrong options / checks: She said that she would be late. | She told me that she would be late. | She told us she would be late.
explanation shown to learner: tell is always followed by a person: She told me / us ...

task: Report this naturally: 'I won't sign it until the lawyer reads it,' the client said. Choose the correct option.
correct answer: The client said he wouldn't sign it until the lawyer had read it.
wrong options / checks: The client said he won't sign it until the lawyer will read it. | The client said I wouldn't sign it until the lawyer reads it. | The client told he wouldn't sign it until the lawyer read it.
explanation shown to learner: won't → wouldn't, I → he, and the earlier action goes back to the past perfect.

task: Report a warning from your doctor: 'You must drink more water.' Start with My doctor said.
correct answer: My doctor said I had to drink more water.
wrong options / checks: must contain: Start with *My doctor said.* ; *must* becomes *had to* (or stays *must*). ; Change *you* to *I.*
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.

task: Choose the correct report. 'Where do you work?' She asked me ___.
correct answer: where I worked
wrong options / checks: where did I work | where do I work | where I work did
explanation shown to learner: In a reported question we use normal word order (subject + verb) and no do / does / did.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Netiešajā jautājumā lieto parasto vārdu secību (teik. priekšmets + darbības vārds) un bez do / does / did.

task: Which word(s) do we use to report a yes/no question?
correct answer: if or whether
wrong options / checks: that | what | do
explanation shown to learner: Do you like jazz? → He asked if (or whether) I liked jazz.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Do you like jazz? → He asked if (vai whether) I liked jazz.

task: Report with backshift: 'What time does the film start?' → She asked what time the film ___. (start)
correct answer: started
explanation shown to learner: Reported question: normal word order, the verb goes back to the past: started.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Netiešais jautājums: parasta vārdu secība, darbības vārds iet atpakaļ pagātnē: started.

task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: He asked me where did I live.
wrong options / checks: He asked me where I lived. | He asked if I wanted a coffee. | She asked whether it was true.
explanation shown to learner: A reported question has statement word order: where I lived, not where did I live.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Netiešajam jautājumam ir teikuma vārdu secība: where I lived, nevis where did I live.

task: A hotel guest asked: 'Is breakfast included?' You report the question. Choose the correct option.
correct answer: The guest asked whether breakfast was included.
wrong options / checks: The guest asked was breakfast included. | The guest asked that breakfast was included. | The guest asked is breakfast included.
explanation shown to learner: Yes/no question: asked + if / whether + subject + verb.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Jā/nē jautājums: asked + if / whether + teik. priekšmets + darbības vārds.

task: Report this question: 'Why are you leaving?' Start with Kate asked me why.
correct answer: Kate asked me why I was leaving.
wrong options / checks: must contain: Start with *Kate asked me why.* ; Statement word order: *why I was leaving.*
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

task: Which sentence reports the request 'Please wait here,' the guard said?
correct answer: The guard told me to wait there.
wrong options / checks: The guard told me wait there. | The guard told me that I wait here. | The guard said me to wait there.
explanation shown to learner: Orders and requests: told / asked + person + to + base verb. Here becomes there.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Rīkojumi un lūgumi: told / asked + persona + to + pamatforma. Here kļūst par there.

task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: she asked me where I lived
explanation shown to learner: Reported question: asked + question word + subject + verb.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Netiešais jautājums: asked + jautājamais vārds + teik. priekšmets + darbības vārds.

task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: he asked if I had finished the report
explanation shown to learner: Yes/no question: asked + if + subject + verb.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Jā/nē jautājums: asked + if + teik. priekšmets + darbības vārds.

task: Which report is correct? 'Can you help me?' she asked.
correct answer: She asked if I could help her.
wrong options / checks: She asked if could I help her. | She asked can I help her. | She asked that I could help her.
explanation shown to learner: can → could, you → I, me → her, and statement word order after if.

task: 'Don't touch that!' the nurse said. Which report is correct?
correct answer: The nurse told me not to touch it.
wrong options / checks: The nurse told me to not touching it. | The nurse told me that I don't touch it. | The nurse said me not to touch it.
explanation shown to learner: A negative order: told + person + not + to + base verb.

task: Report this: 'Could you send me the invoice?' Lena asked.
correct answer: Lena asked me to send her the invoice.
wrong options / checks: also accepted: Lena asked if I could send her the invoice. | Lena asked whether I could send her the invoice. | Lena asked me if I could send her the invoice. | Lena asked me whether I could send her the invoice. | Lena asked me to send the invoice to her. | Lena asked if I would send her the invoice. | Lena asked whether I would send her the invoice. | Lena asked me if I would send her the invoice. | Lena asked me whether I would send her the invoice. | Lena asked if I could send the invoice to her. | Lena asked me if I could send the invoice to her.
explanation shown to learner: A request can be reported with asked + person + to + base verb, or with if / whether + could.

task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: He asked me what time was it.
wrong options / checks: He asked me what time it was. | He asked me when the train left. | He asked me if I knew the way.
explanation shown to learner: In a reported question the subject comes before the verb: what time it was.

task: You report a customer's question to your team: 'How long will the repair take?' the customer asked. Choose the correct option.
correct answer: The customer asked how long the repair would take.
wrong options / checks: The customer asked how long would the repair take. | The customer asked how long will the repair take. | The customer asked how long did the repair take.
explanation shown to learner: Normal word order, and will goes back to would.

task: Report a request you received at work: 'Could you call the supplier?' Start with My manager asked me.
correct answer: My manager asked me to call the supplier.
wrong options / checks: must contain: Start with *My manager asked me.* ; Use *to call*, or *if / whether I could call.*
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.

task: Which report is correct? 'What should I do?' he asked me.
correct answer: He asked me what to do.
wrong options / checks: He asked me what should he do. | He asked me what he does. | He asked me what to doing.
explanation shown to learner: A wh-question with should can be reported with a question word + to + base verb: what to do.

task: What is the difference? A: 'She asked me what to do.' B: 'She asked me what she should do.'
correct answer: There is no difference in meaning. A is shorter.
wrong options / checks: A is about the past and B about the future. | A is a request and B is a question. | B is wrong.
explanation shown to learner: Both are correct. The to-infinitive form is shorter and common in careful English.

task: Report this: 'Where should we meet?' they asked.
correct answer: They asked where to meet.
wrong options / checks: also accepted: They asked where they should meet. | They asked where we should meet.
explanation shown to learner: Question word + to-infinitive, or question word + subject + should.

task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: She asked me whether or not did I agree.
wrong options / checks: She asked me whether or not I agreed. | She asked me whether I agreed or not. | She asked if I agreed.
explanation shown to learner: After whether we use statement word order: whether or not I agreed.

task: You write meeting minutes: 'Has the budget been approved?' Ms Novak asked. Choose the correct option.
correct answer: Ms Novak asked whether the budget had been approved.
wrong options / checks: Ms Novak asked has the budget been approved. | Ms Novak asked whether had the budget been approved. | Ms Novak asked that the budget had been approved.
explanation shown to learner: Yes/no question: asked + whether + subject + verb. The present perfect goes back to the past perfect.

task: Report this question using whether. 'Is the data accurate?' the editor asked. Start with The editor asked whether.
correct answer: The editor asked whether the data was accurate.
wrong options / checks: must contain: Start with *The editor asked whether.* ; Use statement word order and the past: *the data was accurate.*
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.

task: Which sentence reports 'I'm sorry I'm late' with a reporting verb?
correct answer: He apologised for being late.
wrong options / checks: He apologised that he was late. | He apologised to be late. | He apologised of being late.
explanation shown to learner: apologise for + -ing.

task: Match each sentence with the best reporting verb.
correct answer: 'I'll definitely be there on time,' she said. = promised ; 'Don't touch the red button!' he said. = warned ; 'Why don't we try the new café?' she said. = suggested ; 'Yes, I broke the vase,' he said. = admitted
explanation shown to learner: A reporting verb shows what the speaker did: promise, warn, suggest, admit.

task: Report with the verb deny: 'I didn't take your phone,' Max said.
correct answer: Max denied taking my phone.
wrong options / checks: also accepted: Max denied taking your phone. | Max denied that he had taken my phone. | Max denied having taken my phone. | Max denied that he took my phone. | Max denied that he had taken your phone. | Max denied taking the phone. | Max denied that he had taken the phone. | Max denied that he took the phone. | Max denied having taken the phone.
explanation shown to learner: deny + -ing, or deny + that + clause.

task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: She suggested to go by train.
wrong options / checks: She suggested going by train. | She suggested that we go by train. | She suggested we should go by train.
explanation shown to learner: suggest is not followed by to + base verb. Use -ing or that + clause.

task: Report a polite refusal: 'No, I won't work this weekend,' Sam said. Choose the correct option.
correct answer: Sam refused to work that weekend.
wrong options / checks: Sam refused working that weekend. | Sam refused that he works this weekend. | Sam refused me to work that weekend.
explanation shown to learner: refuse + to + base verb.

task: Report this apology with apologise: 'Sorry I forgot the meeting,' Dana said.
correct answer: Dana apologised for forgetting the meeting.
wrong options / checks: must contain: Use *apologised.* ; Use *for* + -ing: *apologised for forgetting.*
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.

task: Which sentence reports 'You broke the printer!' as an accusation?
correct answer: She accused me of breaking the printer.
wrong options / checks: She accused me to break the printer. | She accused me that I broke the printer. | She accused me for breaking the printer.
explanation shown to learner: accuse + person + of + -ing.

task: What is the difference? A: 'He insisted on paying.' B: 'He offered to pay.'
correct answer: A means he would not let others pay. B is a polite offer.
wrong options / checks: A is a polite offer and B is a demand. | Both mean the same. | A is about the past and B about the future.
explanation shown to learner: insist on = refuse to accept a different decision. offer = suggest you will do something.

task: Report with congratulate: 'Well done on winning the award!' Tim said to Jo.
correct answer: Tim congratulated Jo on winning the award.
wrong options / checks: also accepted: Tim congratulated Jo for winning the award.
explanation shown to learner: congratulate + person + on + -ing.

task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: He blamed me for to lose the file.
wrong options / checks: He blamed me for losing the file. | He accused me of losing the file. | He admitted losing the file.
explanation shown to learner: blame + person + for + -ing.

task: Report this concisely and naturally: 'I'm very sorry for the delay, and I will make sure it never happens again,' the manager said. Choose the correct option.
correct answer: The manager apologised for the delay and promised that it would not happen again.
wrong options / checks: The manager said that he was very sorry for the delay and he will make sure it never happens again. | The manager apologised the delay and promised that it will not happen again. | The manager apologised for the delay and promised to that it would not happen again.
explanation shown to learner: A reporting verb says what the speaker did. apologise for + noun, promise + that + clause.

task: Report with a reporting verb. 'It wasn't me who broke it!' said Leo.
correct answer: Leo denied breaking it.
wrong options / checks: must contain: Use a reporting verb such as *denied* or *insisted.*
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.

task: Which sentence reports 'If I were you, I'd take the earlier train,' she said?
correct answer: She advised me to take the earlier train.
wrong options / checks: She suggested me to take the earlier train. | She insisted me to take the earlier train. | She advised to me take the earlier train.
explanation shown to learner: advise + person + to + base verb.

task: 'I'm not going to tell you who did it,' the officer said. Which reporting verb shows he said no?
correct answer: refused
wrong options / checks: promised | admitted | suggested
explanation shown to learner: refuse (to + base verb) means to say no.

task: Report with a reporting verb: 'You really should see a doctor about that cough,' my sister said.
correct answer: My sister advised me to see a doctor about that cough.
wrong options / checks: also accepted: My sister urged me to see a doctor about that cough. | My sister told me to see a doctor about that cough. | My sister encouraged me to see a doctor about that cough. | My sister recommended that I see a doctor about that cough. | My sister recommended that I should see a doctor about that cough. | My sister suggested that I see a doctor about that cough. | My sister suggested that I should see a doctor about that cough. | My sister suggested seeing a doctor about that cough. | My sister suggested I see a doctor about that cough. | My sister suggested I should see a doctor about that cough. | My sister recommended seeing a doctor about that cough. | My sister recommended I see a doctor about that cough. | My sister recommended I should see a doctor about that cough. | My sister advised seeing a doctor about that cough. | My sister advised that I see a doctor about that cough. | My sister advised that I should see a doctor about that cough. | My sister said I should see a doctor about that cough. | My sister said that I should see a doctor about that cough. | My sister told me I should see a doctor about that cough. | My sister told me that I should see a doctor about that cough.
explanation shown to learner: advise / urge / tell / encourage + person + to + base verb; recommend / suggest / advise + -ing or + that + subject + base verb; or said / told me + I should + base verb.

task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: He recommended to reading the report carefully.
wrong options / checks: He recommended reading the report carefully. | He recommended that I read the report carefully. | He advised me to read the report carefully.
explanation shown to learner: Use recommended reading or recommended that I read. Recommended to reading is not a grammatical verb pattern.

task: You report a complaint in formal English: 'The service was terrible and nobody apologised,' the customer said. Choose the correct option.
correct answer: The customer complained that the service had been terrible and that nobody had apologised.
wrong options / checks: The customer complained about the service had been terrible. | The customer complained to be terrible the service. | The customer complained me that the service was terrible.
explanation shown to learner: complain + that + clause. The past goes back to the past perfect.

task: Report with a reporting verb and a noun phrase: 'Thank you for everything you've done,' Mia said to the team.
correct answer: Mia thanked the team for everything they had done.
wrong options / checks: must contain: Use *thanked* (or *expressed thanks*).
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.

topic: Indirect questions (Could you tell me where...)
task: Choose the correct sentence.
correct answer: Could you tell me where the station is?
wrong options / checks: Could you tell me where is the station? | Could you tell me where's the station is? | Could you tell me where the station?
explanation shown to learner: After Could you tell me we use statement word order: where the station is.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Pēc Could you tell me lieto teikuma vārdu secību: where the station is.

topic: Indirect questions (Could you tell me where...)
task: Match each direct question with its polite, indirect form.
correct answer: Where is the toilet? = Do you know where the toilet is? ; What time does the bank open? = Could you tell me what time the bank opens? ; How much is this? = Can you tell me how much this is? ; Is the shop open? = I wonder if the shop is open.
explanation shown to learner: An indirect question starts with a polite phrase, then uses statement word order (no do / does).
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Netiešais jautājums sākas ar pieklājīgu frāzi, tad seko teikuma vārdu secība (bez do / does).

topic: Indirect questions (Could you tell me where...)
task: Where does Anna live? → Do you know where Anna ___?
correct answer: lives
explanation shown to learner: In an indirect question there is no does: where Anna lives.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Netiešajā jautājumā does nav: where Anna lives.

topic: Indirect questions (Could you tell me where...)
task: Which sentence is NOT correct?
correct answer: Do you know what time does the film start?
wrong options / checks: Do you know what time the film starts? | Could you tell me where she lives? | I wonder how much it costs.
explanation shown to learner: No does after the question word in an indirect question: what time the film starts.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Netiešajā jautājumā pēc jautājamā vārda nav does: what time the film starts.

topic: Indirect questions (Could you tell me where...)
task: You ask a stranger for the post office. Choose the most polite option.
correct answer: Excuse me, could you tell me where the post office is?
wrong options / checks: Where is the post office? | Tell me where the post office is. | Excuse me, where is the post office?
explanation shown to learner: A polite phrase + an indirect question sounds softer and more polite.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Pieklājīga frāze + netiešais jautājums skan maigāk un pieklājīgāk.

topic: Indirect questions (Could you tell me where...)
task: Write a polite indirect question to ask a colleague where the meeting room is. Start with Could you tell me.
correct answer: Could you tell me where the meeting room is?
wrong options / checks: must contain: Start with *Could you tell me where.* ; Use statement word order: *where the meeting room is.*
explanation shown to learner: Compare your sentence with the model answer.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Salīdzini savu teikumu ar piemēra atbildi.

topic: Indirect questions (Could you tell me where...)
task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: could you tell me where the station is
explanation shown to learner: Polite phrase + question word + subject + verb.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Pieklājīga frāze + jautājamais vārds + teik. priekšmets + darbības vārds.

topic: Indirect questions (Could you tell me where...)
task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: do you know what time the bank opens
explanation shown to learner: Do you know + question word + subject + verb (no does).
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Do you know + jautājamais vārds + teik. priekšmets + darbības vārds (bez does).

topic: Indirect questions (Could you tell me where...)
task: Choose the correct word: Do you know ___ the shop is open on Sundays?
correct answer: if
wrong options / checks: what | where is | do
explanation shown to learner: For a yes/no question inside another question we use if or whether.
explanation in Latvian (up to B1.2): Jā/nē jautājumam citā jautājumā lieto if vai whether.
